summary: Define four calibrated risk states in the shared result contract
description: Execution brief work unit 2/4. Destination: CallerSignal presents an immediately understandable, uncertainty-honest risk state and has a lawful source-intake foundation without scraping or republishing unlicensed caller databases.

intent_source.text: The current web result makes source confidence visually dominant and the product has no durable source-rights registry, which risks users reading numbering confidence as safety and maintainers treating public caller-report sites as freely reusable data.

execution_brief.destination: CallerSignal presents an immediately understandable, uncertainty-honest risk state and has a lawful source-intake foundation without scraping or republishing unlicensed caller databases.
execution_brief.problem: The current web result makes source confidence visually dominant and the product has no durable source-rights registry, which risks users reading numbering confidence as safety and maintainers treating public caller-report sites as freely reusable data.
execution_brief.chosen_approach: Adopt a hybrid reputation model: present four calibrated risk states across shared contracts and the web; use only official, licensed, or first-party moderated evidence; record source rights before ingestion; never treat missing reports, lookup volume, or a displayed number as proof of safety, guilt, or identity.
non_goals: Scrape, copy, or republish third-party caller-report databases without explicit documented permission.
Ingest real phone numbers, call histories, free-text accusations, or requester identities into the public repository.
Describe no matching reports as proof that answering or returning a call is safe.
Implement public community report ingestion before legal, privacy, moderation, retention, correction, deletion, and abuse controls are approved.

source.recommendation: Adopt a hybrid reputation model: present four calibrated risk states across shared contracts and the web; use only official, licensed, or first-party moderated evidence; record source rights before ingestion; never treat missing reports, lookup volume, or a displayed number as proof of safety, guilt, or identity.

requested_outcomes.text: Every canonical lookup exposes exactly one risk state: official_warning, elevated_signals, no_risk_evidence, or insufficient_evidence, with stable reason codes and an explicit action message.

evidence.summary: Verified by lookup-result schema four-state enum/action contract plus 11 unit tests and integration schema validation.

requested_outcomes.text: Numbering evidence alone produces insufficient_evidence; no_risk_evidence requires at least one current, eligible, risk-capable source checked without a match, while stale, failed, contradictory, unsupported, or rights-restricted risk coverage also produces insufficient_evidence.

evidence.summary: Verified by tests for numbering-only, eligible no-match, stale, failed, contradictory, unsupported, and reuse-restricted coverage.

requested_outcomes.text: No risk state can be raised by lookup popularity or one unverified report, and all existing CLI, MCP, HTTP, and web consumers remain schema-valid.
